# Facts on record

## Execution model

- Two execution paths share parser and phases and differ at the end: the walk interpreter (`fortress file.fss`) and the bytecode compiler (`fortress compile` + `run`) (`repo-internals.md:95-129`).
- The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path; `walk` turns it off and there is no switch to make it run in the interpreter (`repo-internals.md:127`); every "type error" seen from the interpreter is a run-time dispatch failure.
- `fortress typecheck` checks against `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, not the interpreter's prelude, so it is not an oracle for interpreter programs (ledger row 69); making the checker usable on interpreter programs means giving it the interpreter's prelude, which is not a ledger row and not on the worklist as a separate item (it falls under worklist item 2, compiler-path library parity).
- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).
- On microGPT-shaped array code boxing is the dominant representational cost, 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]` in Java models of the program's three kernels, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles: the compiler prelude lacks the array types, with `Array`, `Vector` and `Array3` undefined in `FlatArrays.fsi` (row 305, wider than row 72). On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The order that followed: an `RR64` array type in the compiler library (G2); the two one-line runtime defects (rows 302, 303, since fixed by rung 0); unboxing and `double[]`, designed into the first. A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`258105b3e`; `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The boxing probe's scalar-loop reading, 156× primitive Java with boxing about 2% of it, is of the tree before rung 0's two fixes (rows 302, 303; `53362cb88`); of the costs it named, `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7%) and the representational rest (about 30%) are unaddressed (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The eager debug string of `BaseTask.inATransaction()` is fixed: the message is built only under the `debug` flag (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`; row 302; `53362cb88`; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip is fixed: the literal caches its `double` instead of re-parsing its text in `asRR64()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`; row 303; `53362cb88`; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The benchmark numbers on record from 2026-09-15 (`bench1t` 9.3441 s, `bench1h` 6.0732 s) were taken on a quieter machine; the 2026-09-17 before-run of the same unmodified tree measured 13.0566 s and 8.8159 s, so absolute seconds are not comparable across sessions and only a before/after pair taken in one session is (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `ant compileAll` leaves the bytecode cache holding no library jars: the first `fortress compile` after a rebuild of the compiler clears `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`, and `fortress run` then dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`; the library-order recompile of `repo-internals.md:170-179` restores it, about two minutes (observed 2026-09-17).
- The compiled path's bytecode cache can come up empty after a library-order rebuild that reports exit 0; re-running the same commands one at a time produced the jars (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); whether `nat` parameters are baked into stamped classes is unprobed. Superseded 2026-09-24: a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`).
- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`) gives the identical single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`'s "when we get where clauses working", and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (2026-09-20, rung X). `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it — a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" — and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (2026-09-22, rung C, `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only. A declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. So a comment-only edit to the library is not neutral at the syntax-tree level: rung C's widened three spans (the scalar block's first `-` in both files, `SUFFIX_SUM` in the `.fsi`), besides shifting every position below each insertion, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics must map positions back first (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py`, `remap-lines.py`). No answer changed.
- **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees** (rung I, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, section 4.1): `throw new FortressError((FObject) Driver.getFortressLibrary().getRootValue(name))` from inside a `builtinPrimitive` method reaches `Evaluator.forTry` unchanged (`MethodClosure.java:85-86` has no `catch`) and matches `catch e IntegerOverflow`; `Int.overflow()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:256-259`) is the helper and `WellKnownNames.integerOverflowException` the name. Measured by the 25 `overflows(...)` assertions of `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, whose helper catches nothing but `IntegerOverflow`. Before this rung no native raised one; the interpreter's mapping of every other Java exception is unchanged (`FunctionClosure.java:188-196`), so row 336's division by zero and row 347's `Int.rc` still end the run.

## The checker and the one library

- Only 211 of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 4,518 lines (4.7%) are the 108 `builtinPrimitive` native bindings; the rest is plain Fortress. Whole interpreter library: 427 bindings across nine files. The interpreter's glue classes take the evaluator's boxed values and cannot be reused by the compiled path; the compiler's natives are static Java methods, and `nativeHelpers/` already ships 355 of them, covering about 79 of the 108 by another name. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- `fortress compile Library/FortressLibrary.fss` as it is: 1,417 errors, all in DISAMBIGUATE, all name collisions because both preludes are in scope; an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` made the prelude (a driver over `Shell`'s public entry points, no tracked file changed): disambiguation passes with zero errors; the type checker then reports 92 errors in the library's own apis (36 `X excludes Y but it extends Y`, 26 `types exclude each other`, 26 `Integral[\I\]` bound failures, in the comparison and numeric tower) and then **crashes: `Not yet implemented`** in `STypesUtil.makeInferenceArg` (STypesUtil.scala:546-559) for `nat`, `int`, `bool`, `dim` and `unit` static parameters. Desugar and codegen are never reached. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- **The Scala type checker does not implement `nat` static parameters at all**: a six-line program with a `nat` parameter fails on the compile path (`Not yet implemented` inferred, `ClassCastException` explicit) and runs on the interpreter. The interpreter's library has 81 such declarations, C4's vocabulary 30; `CompilerLibrary` has one, the empty `Matrix`. So the sized-array vocabulary cannot pass the compile path's checker today, and the static dimension checking the `nat` design promises is not implemented anywhere. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- **Between the interpreter's library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation** (2026-09-20, `perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen.md`, the library pushed through DESUGAR and CODEGEN with the checker's failures caught per top-level declaration, validated on `CompilerLibrary.fss` where the method reproduces the ordinary compile exactly): of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 446 top-level declarations the checker passes 237 clean, reports errors on 97 and crashes on 112 (81 `makeInferenceArg` nyi, 29 `TraitType→IntExpr`, the `nat` gap); DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE then report zero diagnostics on all of it; CODEGEN emits 275 and refuses 313, of which only **5 are on declarations the checker checked clean** (four a numeric static argument, one a method call on an intersection-typed receiver); the rest are missing annotations on unchecked declarations (227), the two missing visitors `Juxt` (53) and `Label` (1), `nat` static arguments (14), malformed overload sets (7); `canCompile` refused nothing and no native binding was missing. Two obstacles the earlier counts did not show: the compile path's own `extends Object` pre-desugaring (`Shell.java:371-386`) adds 712 of the 960 checker errors in the prelude apis and 618 of 1,204 in the component, rejecting every generic instantiated at a tuple type, more than the 93 tower errors; and overload dispatch generation does not terminate on this library's exclusion graph (1,046 s, stopped by hand), so it was switched off for the measurement.
- **The `nat` plan's minimal design works as a shadow, and the road is three batches, not one** (2026-09-21, `perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md`, `shadow.patch`, 22 captures; Pavol approved the shadow, decision F questions 1-3). Over `FortressLibrary` under `WorldFlip` the `makeInferenceArg` crash is gone and the count goes 93 → 117, all 24 new in `NativeArray`, the api the crash had hidden: 22 pre-existing and now reachable, 2 caused by the new rule (`subarray`'s return type on `ImmutableArray1`/`Array1` against `ReadableArray1`, `.fsi:1411-1413`) and suspect. `FlatArrays`/`FlatArrays2`: no nat-related error left in their own declarations. Corrections to the plan: the api has 25 declarations with a dead size, not six, and their line range is three lines early.
- **The shadow's two `subarray` errors were the rule's, fixed in two lines, and the checker's slowdown is the tree's own** (2026-09-21, `perf-probes/nat/followup.md`, captures `followup/`). A size left unsolved after comparing two declarations' return types was counted as a failure (`Formula.imp`, `Formula.scala:168`, via `OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule` and `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:145`); with an all-size residue read as true, the library count goes 117 → 115 and the error set equals the run with size equality switched off, so the equality rule causes zero library errors; the denied shape was `Vector`'s, `Matrix`'s and C4's slicing, so the rule carries it. # Facts on record

## Execution model

- Two execution paths share parser and phases and differ at the end: the walk interpreter (`fortress file.fss`) and the bytecode compiler (`fortress compile` + `run`) (`repo-internals.md:95-129`).
- The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path; `walk` turns it off and there is no switch to make it run in the interpreter (`repo-internals.md:127`); every "type error" seen from the interpreter is a run-time dispatch failure.
- `fortress typecheck` checks against `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, not the interpreter's prelude, so it is not an oracle for interpreter programs (ledger row 69); making the checker usable on interpreter programs means giving it the interpreter's prelude, which is not a ledger row and not on the worklist as a separate item (it falls under worklist item 2, compiler-path library parity).
- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).
- On microGPT-shaped array code boxing is the dominant representational cost, 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]` in Java models of the program's three kernels, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles: the compiler prelude lacks the array types, with `Array`, `Vector` and `Array3` undefined in `FlatArrays.fsi` (row 305, wider than row 72). On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The order that followed: an `RR64` array type in the compiler library (G2); the two one-line runtime defects (rows 302, 303, since fixed by rung 0); unboxing and `double[]`, designed into the first. A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`258105b3e`; `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The boxing probe's scalar-loop reading, 156× primitive Java with boxing about 2% of it, is of the tree before rung 0's two fixes (rows 302, 303; `53362cb88`); of the costs it named, `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7%) and the representational rest (about 30%) are unaddressed (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The eager debug string of `BaseTask.inATransaction()` is fixed: the message is built only under the `debug` flag (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`; row 302; `53362cb88`; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip is fixed: the literal caches its `double` instead of re-parsing its text in `asRR64()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`; row 303; `53362cb88`; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The benchmark numbers on record from 2026-09-15 (`bench1t` 9.3441 s, `bench1h` 6.0732 s) were taken on a quieter machine; the 2026-09-17 before-run of the same unmodified tree measured 13.0566 s and 8.8159 s, so absolute seconds are not comparable across sessions and only a before/after pair taken in one session is (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `ant compileAll` leaves the bytecode cache holding no library jars: the first `fortress compile` after a rebuild of the compiler clears `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`, and `fortress run` then dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`; the library-order recompile of `repo-internals.md:170-179` restores it, about two minutes (observed 2026-09-17).
- The compiled path's bytecode cache can come up empty after a library-order rebuild that reports exit 0; re-running the same commands one at a time produced the jars (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); whether `nat` parameters are baked into stamped classes is unprobed. Superseded 2026-09-24: a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`).
- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`) gives the identical single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`'s "when we get where clauses working", and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (2026-09-20, rung X). `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it — a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" — and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (2026-09-22, rung C, `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only. A declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. So a comment-only edit to the library is not neutral at the syntax-tree level: rung C's widened three spans (the scalar block's first `-` in both files, `SUFFIX_SUM` in the `.fsi`), besides shifting every position below each insertion, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics must map positions back first (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py`, `remap-lines.py`). No answer changed.
- **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees** (rung I, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, section 4.1): `throw new FortressError((FObject) Driver.getFortressLibrary().getRootValue(name))` from inside a `builtinPrimitive` method reaches `Evaluator.forTry` unchanged (`MethodClosure.java:85-86` has no `catch`) and matches `catch e IntegerOverflow`; `Int.overflow()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:256-259`) is the helper and `WellKnownNames.integerOverflowException` the name. Measured by the 25 `overflows(...)` assertions of `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, whose helper catches nothing but `IntegerOverflow`. Before this rung no native raised one; the interpreter's mapping of every other Java exception is unchanged (`FunctionClosure.java:188-196`), so row 336's division by zero and row 347's `Int.rc` still end the run.

## The checker and the one library

- Only 211 of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 4,518 lines (4.7%) are the 108 `builtinPrimitive` native bindings; the rest is plain Fortress. Whole interpreter library: 427 bindings across nine files. The interpreter's glue classes take the evaluator's boxed values and cannot be reused by the compiled path; the compiler's natives are static Java methods, and `nativeHelpers/` already ships 355 of them, covering about 79 of the 108 by another name. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- `fortress compile Library/FortressLibrary.fss` as it is: 1,417 errors, all in DISAMBIGUATE, all name collisions because both preludes are in scope; an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` made the prelude (a driver over `Shell`'s public entry points, no tracked file changed): disambiguation passes with zero errors; the type checker then reports 92 errors in the library's own apis (36 `X excludes Y but it extends Y`, 26 `types exclude each other`, 26 `Integral[\I\]` bound failures, in the comparison and numeric tower) and then **crashes: `Not yet implemented`** in `STypesUtil.makeInferenceArg` (STypesUtil.scala:546-559) for `nat`, `int`, `bool`, `dim` and `unit` static parameters. Desugar and codegen are never reached. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- **The Scala type checker does not implement `nat` static parameters at all**: a six-line program with a `nat` parameter fails on the compile path (`Not yet implemented` inferred, `ClassCastException` explicit) and runs on the interpreter. The interpreter's library has 81 such declarations, C4's vocabulary 30; `CompilerLibrary` has one, the empty `Matrix`. So the sized-array vocabulary cannot pass the compile path's checker today, and the static dimension checking the `nat` design promises is not implemented anywhere. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16.
- **Between the interpreter's library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation** (2026-09-20, `perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen.md`, the library pushed through DESUGAR and CODEGEN with the checker's failures caught per top-level declaration, validated on `CompilerLibrary.fss` where the method reproduces the ordinary compile exactly): of `FortressLibrary.fss`'s 446 top-level declarations the checker passes 237 clean, reports errors on 97 and crashes on 112 (81 `makeInferenceArg` nyi, 29 `TraitType→IntExpr`, the `nat` gap); DESUGAR and OVERLOADREWRITE then report zero diagnostics on all of it; CODEGEN emits 275 and refuses 313, of which only **5 are on declarations the checker checked clean** (four a numeric static argument, one a method call on an intersection-typed receiver); the rest are missing annotations on unchecked declarations (227), the two missing visitors `Juxt` (53) and `Label` (1), `nat` static arguments (14), malformed overload sets (7); `canCompile` refused nothing and no native binding was missing. Two obstacles the earlier counts did not show: the compile path's own `extends Object` pre-desugaring (`Shell.java:371-386`) adds 712 of the 960 checker errors in the prelude apis and 618 of 1,204 in the component, rejecting every generic instantiated at a tuple type, more than the 93 tower errors; and overload dispatch generation does not terminate on this library's exclusion graph (1,046 s, stopped by hand), so it was switched off for the measurement.
- **The `nat` plan's minimal design works as a shadow, and the road is three batches, not one** (2026-09-21, `perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md`, `shadow.patch`, 22 captures; Pavol approved the shadow, decision F questions 1-3). With the five checker files copied beside the tree and the third solver track added: sizes inferred, written out, and the spec's `makeVector` shape compile clean; a mismatch is refused; arithmetic in a size is refused as ill-formed; `bool`/`dim`/`unit` give a checker error naming the kind; the five nat-using compiler tests are byte-identical stock and shadow. Over `FortressLibrary` under `WorldFlip` the `makeInferenceArg` crash is gone and the count goes 93 → 117, all 24 new in `NativeArray`, the api the crash had hidden: 22 pre-existing and now reachable, 2 caused by the new rule (`subarray`'s return type on `ImmutableArray1`/`Array1` against `ReadableArray1`, `.fsi:1411-1413`) and suspect. `FlatArrays`/`FlatArrays2`: no nat-related error left in their own declarations. Both of decision F's stop conditions were met: the second crash is in Java as well as Scala (`AbstractMethodChecker.scala:83`, one line; `compiler/codegen/FnNameInfo.java:162-196` via `Functionals.scala:606`, any method on a nat-parameterized receiver), so the plan's "no Java" is void; and a compiled sized program fails to load (`NoClassDefFoundError: 3$RTTIc`, `MethodInstantiater.rttiReference:124-138`), because `isOprKind` (`Naming.java:103`) is the only static-argument kind the run time has, so sizes need a run-time kind. Not settled: the fate of the 112 crashing declarations (the per-declaration run slowed to about seven minutes for `trait Number` alone and was stopped at 46 of 446); the two suspect `subarray` errors; the gate cannot see a classpath shadow. Corrections to the plan: the api has 25 declarations with a dead size, not six, and their line range is three lines early.
- **The shadow's two `subarray` errors were the rule's, fixed in two lines, and the checker's slowdown is the tree's own** (2026-09-21, `perf-probes/nat/followup.md`, captures `followup/`). A size left unsolved after comparing two declarations' return types was counted as a failure (`Formula.imp`, `Formula.scala:168`, via `OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule` and `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:145`); with an all-size residue read as true, the library count goes 117 → 115 and the error set equals the run with size equality switched off, so the equality rule causes zero library errors; the denied shape was `Vector`'s, `Matrix`'s and C4's slicing, so the rule carries it. The slowdown: 87 % of 39,287 JFR samples in `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` from `TypeAnalyzer.parents` (`:722`) and `excludesClause` (`:747`), neither memoized and the second recursing over every supertrait, no sample in the size track; a fourteen-line memo makes the shadow faster than the stock tree (whole library 32 s → 13 s against the tree's 21 s; the per-declaration run finishes 446 of 446 in 307 s against the tree's 554 s). The fate of the 112 crashing declarations, now measured: 263 clean / 142 with own errors / 41 crashes under the shadow against the tree's 236 / 98 / 112; all 81 `NI.nyi` gone; 36 of the 41 left are `FnNameInfo.java`. Not settled: five declarations clean under the tree report one error under the shadow (`FortressLibrary.fss:129, :2248, :2594, :3064, :3151`), three of one shape (a `__bigOperatorSugar` body whose return type is taken from the nullary api overload, `.fsi:96` not `:98`, no size in them) and `__builtinFactory2` at `:2594` a likely true positive (branches `Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\]` and `__DefaultArray2[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1\]` join only under its own `if b0=0 AND b1=0` guard); the two-line relaxation is coarser than keeping escaped sizes existential in `OverloadingOracle.scala`; the memo needs a home on `TraitTable`; no suite run.

Probes, the five nat compiler tests and the whole-unit count (115) unchanged; `NatExtends1` now passes the checker and stops at `CodeGen.java:5793`. The mangled name for a sized receiver keeps the size as its own symbol (`NamingCzar.forIntRef` `:1894-1897`, `forIntBase` `:1889-1892`). The load failure `NoClassDefFoundError: 3$RTTIc` is asked for at `MethodInstantiater.rttiReference:117-138` and `CodeGen.generateTypeReference:5784-5793`; a symbol needs no descriptor (the template holds `Box⟦k⟧$RTTIc`), only literals reach the loader; stamping `<n>$RTTIc` per literal (an ASM tool, 36 lines) plus a 17-line `runtimeValues/RTTIsize.java` makes `pNat1`, `pNat2`, `pNatMeth`, `pNatGenMeth` compile, load and print 7. Also: `typecase` is broken for every generic, sized or not (`pTypeCase` fails identically with the shadow off); read again 2026-09-24 (`reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md` § 2), both programs have row 340's shape, a `typecase` as a whole function body whose clauses need a coercion, so the failure says nothing about generics and whether a type test sees a size is open; `bool`/`dim`/`unit` keep both latent bugs; no suite run. 82	- `Vector[\T extends Number, nat s0\]` and `Matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]` are the only sized array traits; `Array3[\T, nat b0, nat s0, …\]` carries no algebraic trait (row 292; `FortressLibrary.fsi:1465, 1583, 1657` since the library commits of climb batches 3 and 3.5).
83	- `Vector` and `Matrix` inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero` from `AdditiveGroup`, nothing else; `×` reaches no array by design because juxtaposition is the inner product and the array traits exclude `AnyMultiplicativeRing` (rows 64, 109, 293); a carrier that extends the ring is accepted unchecked, changes juxtaposition to elementwise and breaks `+` (vocabulary review v02, v02b).
84	- The library's products are declared with shared `nat`s (`Matrix[\T,n,m\]` × `Matrix[\T,m,p\]`, `FortressLibrary.fsi:1508-1516`); C4's own products were not, which is habit; the focused base's `FlatArrays2` states them (twelve declarations including the per-rank elementwise `×` and `/`, 25 of 29 nats agreeing; 39 declarations), and a wrong-shape call is refused at dispatch, uncatchable for an overloaded name (row 83), as a unification error naming the nat for an unoverloaded one (`apl/mg/checks/mismatch_probe.out`).
85	- Two declarations of one name differing only in the element type, or a rank-specialised declaration beside an index-generic one, are refused at load ("at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"; `apl/mg/checks/model_run.out.0`, `elemwise_nat_probe.out.0`); two apis' overloads of one name are checked as one family, so two vocabularies cannot stand in one component (`diag_fwd_two_vocabularies_rejected.out.0`).
86	- The shipped `RR64` does not satisfy the specification's algebraic bound `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` (vocabulary review, probe `v04b_groupbound.out.0`); `T extends Number` is the bound that works for every element type and rank (row 295).
87	- The library's scalar-extension block for `+ - MIN MAX` over arrays is generic since `02d09a39f` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4511-4521`, `.fsi:2550-2560`); no reshape, plane, gather, outer product or ravel exists in the library (vocabulary review, section A).
88	- An array is a trait with `get`/`put`; a view is an object implementing it over other storage, the language's own idiom; the library's row slice `m[i,:]` costs 5× a six-line user view; a diagonal as a `Matrix` view costs 13-54× the operator (vocabulary review v20, v07); a subtype of `Matrix` that overrides `mul` gets its specialised product through the library's own operators, which forward to `mul` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2627-2633`), at the operator's cost and with no api line, since the interpreter dispatches the method on the receiver's run-time type (2026-09-25, `run-c4/probes/vocabulary/diag-override.md`; ledger row 299).
89	- The element type is `Number` only for `Vector`/`Matrix` (row 24); irrelevant to numeric microGPT, decisive for Run B's autodiff value and for APL characters.

91	## The specification and the repository's lineage
92	
93	- **Citing `Specification/library/apis/*.tex` as an independent standard is circular.** `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31` says in the team's own words that Part Library "is largely automatically generated from the API code for the libraries themselves" and that the libraries are "presently in a state of flux", so `library/apis/CompilerBuiltin.tex` is a rendering of `CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and cannot justify an edit to that same file. Two rung reports cited it as the published api or the spec's shape. The prose chapters of `Specification/basic/` and `basic-lib/` are the standard; the api renderings are not. Sharper still (2026-09-19, batch 1's record worker): the rendered `library/apis/*.tex` files are not in the tree at all, they are generated at spec-build time from the `.fsi` sources (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27,39`), so the `(api listing)` citations of ledger rows 314 and 316 and of `library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31` name paths that cannot be opened; the `(api listing)` convention should cite the `.fsi` line instead. Source: the conformance review of the eight rungs, 2026-09-17, `reviews/rung-conformance-1-4.md` and `-5-8.md`, verified in that session.
94	- The in-repo `Specification/` is the later draft with the implementers' notes; `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is 1.0. Searches are made in the draft. Superseded 2026-09-16 by `map/spec-to-implementation.md` §1.2: the sources under `Specification-1.0-frozen/` are a byte-identical copy of the same draft in 202 of 208 files (the five differences are the revival's `fortress.tex` restyling, three `.pl` generators, and one stray `\tracingcommands` line); only `fortress.1.0.pdf` beside them is the 1.0 artefact. There is one prose to search, the draft, and it is 596 pages against the PDF's 262.
95	- `palimondo/fortress` is a 2018 GitHub fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository: 5,397 trunk commits, root `72ae6881b` (2007-01-04), tip `a874948ac` (2012-08-31), twelve relic branches, the `1.0` tag; the conversion cut 146 parent links (`research/authorship.md:14-22`). The third-party Java 9 port is one squashed commit (`eab48aa6d`) sharing no history with this tree; `8fe1daa8f` (2026-08-18) copied 1,506 of its files onto `a874948ac`, most of it since removed or redone; `clean-ladder` (`8332bd34f`) is a rebuild on `a874948ac` with no graft that never replaced `main`, so `main` still descends from `8fe1daa8f` (the work went on pushing the grafted line to `main` after the rebuild, no rename or merge ever happened) and its tree owes the port one running piece, the `FTypeArrayList` fix for the JDK 8 `TreeSet` crash (`clean-ladder` fixes it in two lines), plus dead files, cosmetic lines and the habit of tracking the generated sources (verified against `clean-ladder`, `lineage.md`). CLAUDE.md's opening sentence said otherwise from `446836590` until corrected; the files that still repeat it are listed in `lineage.md`.
96	
97	## The territory map
98	
99	- Tasks and transactions are implemented twice, `interpreter/evaluator/` and `runtimeSystem/`, independently (B.11). Row 302's fix is in the compiled world's copy only.
100	- `import java` also works on the interpreter path through `ForeignComponentWrapper` + `ClosureMaker`; no test uses it (B.12). Corrected 2026-09-20 (`perf-probes/prelude/import-java-interpreter.md`): wired and unfinished, it does not work; four gaps, all on the interpreter's side: `NamingCzar.fortLib` is fixed to the builtin api, which declares none of `ZZ32`/`RR64`/`JavaString` in that world (`NamingCzar.java:294-295`); a second `import java` from one package falls through `Driver.ensureApiImplemented` to a `ClassCastException` (`Driver.java:464-466`, "temp hack till we knit in natives properly"); the foreign name is never rewritten (`ForeignComponentWrapper.java:31,38`) and `BaseEnv.java:531-533` bugs on the qualified reference; and `ClosureMaker` emits a call into the compiler's `nativewrapper_cache`, which the interpreter neither writes nor loads. So one binding file cannot serve both worlds; the one-library variant is one shared text with one small builtin component per world behind a single api, which makes the api-to-differently-named-component link (ledger row 320's class-name half, `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`) live work.
101	- Codegen refuses any declaration carrying a where clause or a contract (`CodeGen.java:2937, :2941, :4076, :4078, :4983, :4985`); not in the ledger (flagged, Pavol's call). `atomic <expr>` has no visitor, `atomic do … end` compiles; `spawn`, `label`/`exit`, object expressions, array literals and comprehensions, local function declarations have no visitor (`spec-to-implementation.md` §3).
102	- The checker (`IndexBuilder.scala:187-189`) refuses `type` aliases, `test` and `property` on both paths. Coercion is the one mechanism the compiler path has and the interpreter does not (no `Coercion`/`coerce` under `interpreter/`; row 19).
103	- **A generic object referenced without its static arguments is a static error on the compiled path, and the checker never consults the expected type for it** (2026-09-19, `explorations/compiler-probes/maybe-inference/inference.md`): `b: Box[\ZZ32\] = Box` fails with `Ill-formed type: Box`; a bare `Empty` as a call argument or a field default fails with `T is not in the kind env`, an internal `bug()` from `TypeAnalyzer.scala:766` reported at the declaration's span; the same forms with the static argument written compile and run on both paths. The decision is in the checker's `SVarRef` case, `typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:624-641`, whose `:639-640` keeps the uninstantiated type under the team's own `TODO: handle missing static args`; static-argument inference exists only for arrows (`STypesUtil.scala:912-930`, called from application and coercion), and a parametric empty case reached by `coerce` still fails bare. Under `walk` the same forms are `InterpreterBug: Couldn't figure out Empty[\T\](uninstantiated) <: Opt[\ZZ32\]`. Consequence for row 331: a parametric `Nothing[\T\]` would serve the corpus's `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` and never the specification's bare `= Nothing`; the non-parametric object plus `coerce` that the prelude uses is the only shape that compiles, so `Maybe` stays as landed. Incidental: `typecase` over a user-declared generic object crashes code generation (`Error trying to close method scope`, `CodeGen.java:2802`), row 340. Corrected the same day by the minimal reproducer (`compiler-probes/maybe-inference/probes/TcPlain.fss`): neither the generic object nor `typecase` alone is the trigger; a `typecase` used directly as a function or method body whose value needs an implicit coercion (`IntLiteral` to a declared `ZZ32`) makes ASM's stack-map frame computation fail (`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` under `MethodWriter.visitMaxs`, relabelled by the `catch (Throwable)` at `CodeGen.java:2801-2802`); wrapped in `do … end` the same body compiles, and every gated use of the shape returns `()` so never reaches the coercion.
104	- The gate: two corpora, hand-ported, sharing no file name; only `parser_tests/` is read by both; no test compares the paths on one program; interpreter tests pass on "no exception and no `fail` in output" (`FileTests.java:367-371`), compiler run tests on exit code plus `PASS`. `fortress.unittests.noopt=true` (`default_repository/configuration:51`) hides 226 tests and leaves the 43-file bytecode optimizer with zero. Every `testSystem` shard runs `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` (`build.xml:1184`), so no gated test sees concurrency; `TransactionJUTest`'s multi-threaded half is commented out (`TestTask.java:43-44`). No `nat`-parameterised program is compiled or run; the cache round trip is not asserted (`ASTJUTest.java:654`). 121 `.fss` inside green directories are dark; `linker_tests`, `compiler_regressions`, `BirdyLib`, the `not_working_*` directories are orphaned (`map/test-coverage.md`).
105	
106	## The container
107	
108	- The process cost of the climbs and the batches — the eight-rung climb's wall clock and its gate share, the limits of parallelism on this box, and each batch's agents, tokens, tool calls and span — is measured in `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md`, `coordinator/repair-batch-review.md` and the batch records; the conclusions it produced are in `POSITIONS.md` and in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`, and the entries themselves are in `FACTS-history.md`.
109	- The Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling kills long runs; check runs go under the `Monitor` tool (1800000 ms), sequential, nothing else running when a number is to be kept.
110	- The disk allowance fills with parser-generation temp directories: every run that imports a grammar generates a Rats! parser into a fresh `/tmp/fortress<random>rats` directory (`RatsUtil.getTempDir`, `syntax_abstractions/rats/RatsUtil.java:138-146`, via `IOUtil.createAndMarkTempDirectory`), 5.8 MB each, never deleted; 723 of them (4.2 GB) filled the allowance on 2026-09-15 and broke a worker's tool output mid-run ("no space left on device"). Deficit until fixed at the source (an edit under the sealed tree, or a `deleteOnExit`); mitigation in our tree: `explorations/experiment/env.sh` removes them when sourced, and `df` must be checked before any long run.
111	- The Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling; `Monitor` for long runs (the microGPT-runs entry above).
112	- A container can be lost outright: the coordinating session of 2026-09-17 (`bdff267d-…`) died mid-workflow and could not be re-provisioned, because the branch it was created from was no longer found on the remote. Recovery moved into the blinded run's container, which already had the checkout and toolchain. Cost: four workflow agents (~798k tokens), their worktrees, and the 13 hours after the last transcript snapshot at 20:31. Everything through `2ab1d6d8` was pushed and safe, and `REPAIR-BATCH.md` kept the batch runnable. Mechanism, the three traps and the recovery procedure: `explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md`.
113	- The transcript backup fires on the main session's Stop, not on any agent's completion, and swallows all errors: a session inside one long turn is not being backed up and a failed push is silent. Workflow-agent transcripts were outside its globs until 2026-09-18; oversized transcripts now split at 64 MiB, and the wrapper packs loose objects because the clone ships `gc.auto=0`.
114	- **The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box** (measured 2026-09-18, four one-command agents in one `parallel()`: agents 0 and 1 started 19:14:08, agents 2 and 3 at 19:14:31 after the first pair finished at 19:14:23; `batched-climb-plan.md` §2). `model: 'opus'` in `agent()` resolves to a fixed model identifier, readable in each agent transcript's `message.model` field and not written here (protocol §4); an agent with no `model` inherits the session's. A subagent's floor is about 45k tokens before it does anything (183k for the four). Prompt caching across parallel agents covers the system prompt and tools only (33,022 tokens read by agents 1–3) and not the first user message (11,010 written by each), because a cache read lands only at a breakpoint the harness placed and a shared prefix inside one message is not one.
115	- The VM can be restarted under a live session with the disk intact: 2026-09-18 23:22 UTC, 25 minutes into the repair batch's re-run, kernel build string fc-v33 → fc-v37, one JVM running (16 GB, no swap, 4 CPUs: not a memory death). Worktrees, uncommitted edits and agent transcripts survived; the Workflow run and its agents did not, and a run is relaunched, never resumed; the `wip/` branches held every pushed milestone (`remote-container.md` § The 2026-09-18 restart).
116	- **A user interrupt of the coordinating session's turn kills a background Workflow run** (2026-09-19): climb batch 1's first run, `wf_a29fd04b-a9a`, launched 07:15 UTC, lost both its rung agents at 07:46:42, the second Pavol's interrupt cut the turn that a check-in trigger had just started; both agent transcripts end at that timestamp mid-work, no result line reached the journal, and the harness no longer knew the task. The Agent tool's workers are not affected (the review worker launched after the interrupt ran to completion). The `wip/` branches held F's three and M's three milestones and M's worktree its uncommitted report, so the relaunch at 08:25 from the same base continued under the prefix's continuation clause. Cost: about 40 minutes of two workers. Rule: while a Workflow runs, a check-in must not be interrupted mid-turn; and a batch is relaunched, never resumed, after any such death.
117	- **A manual compaction issued between turns leaves a running Workflow alive** (found 2026-09-19 by a worker in the archived transcript of session `bdff267d`, `transcripts` branch, parts file `001.jsonl`): the eight-rung climb's run `wf_73833dfb-d25` (launched 2026-09-17 06:00:57 UTC) survived two `/compact` commands, boundaries 10:47:33 (442,504 tokens before, 130 s) and 14:25:25 (177,831 tokens, 153 s), both typed while the session sat between turns; rung 5's commit landed 84 s after the first boundary, rungs 6-8 and the final re-run followed, and the run's completion notification arrived 14:39:09 with all eight rungs. This container's three compactions (09-18 18:38, 22:54; 09-19 06:38) coincided with no run. So the rule is: compact between turns, never send during a turn; the 09-19 death was a mid-turn interrupt, not a compaction. Caveat: that run's journal and agent transcripts are not in the backup, so the agents' survival is inferred from their commits and the session's own status turns.
118	- **`explorations/experiment/env.sh` is the one script every probe and gate runner sources, and it is verified from its new home** (2026-09-24, after `7bc8177a3` moved `experiment/` under `explorations/`): it derives `FORTRESS_HOME` from its own location two levels up, and re-running the two shadow experiments that source it, `reviews/mie-probes/forest/forest-run.sh` (423 s) and `perf-probes/nat/runtime/run-all.sh` (669 s), reproduced every committed count and probe output (`checker-count.txt`'s six counts, stock 103 and forest 37 among them, and captures r1-r5 byte-identical); the only differences were dates, timings and line numbers shifted by the library commits `c2b4e2c95` and `d6faad28f` made after the captures. astra's scripts keep their own `experiment/` paths, which name astra's tree.
119	
120	## The ledger
121	
122	- Rows are never renumbered or moved, and the reports cite them by number; the counts by kind are derived by script in the ledger's counts (`fortress-gap-ledger.md:714`), and the revival worklist (46 items, `fortress-gap-ledger.md:574`) and `apl/lessons.md` are the two derived views. Five cost rows sit in section 15; whether they get a section of their own is Pavol's call.

- The checker-count stage's table, `gate/checker-count.txt`, lands with every batch beside the gate's `summary.txt`; `last_landed_checker_count` finds the last landed table (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:947-951`), 103 since climb batch 3 (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-3/gate/checker-count.txt`, `99c4715ac`), and the next batch's count may only fall from it or declare its rise (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-3/RECORD.md`, "The landing") (full entry in FACTS-history.md).

## The harness and the gate

- The ladder-regression stage's baseline is `compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/pass-list.txt`, whose files are compiled and run, and the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs are held at their phase, disambiguate, as recorded in `compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/microgpt-phase.md`, compiled only (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:890-892`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- The harness's `run_out_WIcontains` key is whitespace-insensitive containment, runs of whitespace collapsed in both the output and the expected string as `_WImatches` does (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:155-163`, `:181-188`; `a0fcf0a96`). A key `generalTestFailed` does not know sets no check, and a `run_out` with no check falls to the default, stdout contains `pass` or `PASS` (`:276-282`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).
- **The gate's thread count is pinned in the build file, not in the calling shell** (2026-09-19, `build.xml:947` in the `fastTrack` macro, beside `systemShard`'s own at `:1188`): `<env key="FORTRESS_THREADS" value="1"/>`. Before it, `fastTrack` set only `FORTRESS_CACHES`; the forked JUnit JVM and the per-test subprocess inherited the caller's environment (`FileTests.java:482-486`), `getNumThreads` otherwise takes `floor(nproc/2)` (`FortressExecutable.java:37-44`), and the `1` came from `explorations/experiment/env.sh:6` — so `ant testFast` from a shell that had not sourced `env.sh`, which is what CI and Pavol's machine would do, ran `compiler_tests` at a different count and proved something else. Verified directly: with `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` exported in the calling shell, `ant -v testFast` logs `Setting environment variable: FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for each of the four `fastTrack` forks. `env.sh`'s line is now a convenience rather than the definition.
- **`ant compileAll` deletes a tracked file** (2026-09-20, rung X, and reproduced at the gather stage). `compileAll` depends on `compileCommon` (`build.xml:539`), which depends on `cleanCache` (`:715`), which deletes `default_repository/caches` entire (`:42,356-359`) — including the tracked `global.map`, the linker's persisted `RepoState` (`linker/RepoState.java:176`). Every tree that runs `ant compileAll` therefore shows `D default_repository/caches/global.map` afterwards, and a `git add -A` at that moment commits the deletion; restore it with `git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map`.
- **An `XXX*.fss` in the interpreter corpus IS a gated expected-failure test** (established 2026-09-20 at the gather stage of climb batch 2, against rung W's record, which said the opposite and whose report is corrected). `ProjectFortress/tests/` holds 383 `.fss` and no `.test` file, and `FileTests.interpreterSuite("tests", true, false)` (`FileTests.java:768`) passes `expect_failure=false` — but that argument is the **fifth**, `knownFailure`; the `InterpreterTest` constructor at `:710-711` supplies the sixth itself, `super(path, d, s, unexpected_only, knownFailure, s.startsWith("XXX"))`, so `shouldFail` there comes from the file name, it is the same `final boolean shouldFail` field (`:69-70`, `:91`) that `:384` branches on, and `:400-402` fails the suite when such a file starts passing. 55 `XXX*.fss` already live in that directory, `XXXImportImportCollision.fss` and `XXXImportLocalCollision.fss` among them, and their api pairs come from `ProjectFortress/test_library/` (21 `.fsi`), so such a test needs neither a `.test` file nor a new api directory. What is true of `compiler_tests/` is the narrower constraint rung X recorded: there the mechanism runs through `TestTest`, and an `XXX*.test` cannot carry a `run_out_contains` key unless the failing run still prints the marker. The shape for a compiles-but-fails-at-run-time defect in that corpus is two `.test` files over one component, a plain-named one driving `link` and an `XXX`-named one driving `run`; rung B measured it and the gather used it for row 348's test, showing it go red on a deliberate local fix at `FileTests.java:587-589`.
- **The `XXX` expected-failure mechanism in `compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` can express a compile-stage failure only, and a run-time defect needs two `.test` files** (2026-09-20, rung B). `shouldFail` comes from the `.test` file name (`FileTests.java:932`) and the same flag reaches every stage the file drives (`:1052-1059`, `:1063-1069`), so an `XXX` file that carries `link` or `compile` demands that the compile fail (`:384-404`, message at `:402`); and a `TestTest` fails on an unsatisfied `run_out_*` verdict whatever `shouldFail` says (`:534-539`, `:583-585`), with `pass`/`PASS` demanded by default when no check is set (`:276-282`). Of the 224 `XXX*.test` files that were in `compiler_tests/` before this batch, 223 drive `compile`, one drives `link`, none drives `run`. A compiles-but-crashes defect is therefore gated as two `.test` files over one component — a plain-named one driving `link`, an `XXX`-named one driving `run` with a marker the failing run does print — which is what rung B did and showed going red on a deliberate fix (`compile-ladder/rung-tryatomic/raw/junit-xxx-expected.txt`, `raw/junit-xxx-goes-red.txt`), and what the gather reused for rung W's row 348.
- **A thrown `CompilerError` takes a third path through the test harness, keyed on the `tests=` name, with check stream `compile_exception_*`** (2026-09-20, the repair after climb batch 2's merged-diff review). A `sayWhat` wall returns a `CompilerError` (`CodeGen.java:1551-1553`), which is a `RuntimeException` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/CompilerError.java:16`) and so is caught by neither clause of `Shell.compileWithErrorHandling` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:904-915`, `StaticError` and `ProgramError` only); `Shell.subMain` declares `throws Throwable` (`Shell.java:395-396`), so in the harness it propagates out of `justTheTest` (`FileTests.java:689-692`) to the `catch (Throwable ex)` at `FileTests.java:341`. There the expected-failure branch keys on `f.contains("XXX")` (`:346`) with `f = join(_dir, _name)` (`:82`) and `_name` the `.test` file's `tests=` value (`:1052-1059`) — **not** the `.test` file name of `:932` that the 224 printed-error files use through `:384-404`, so the `XXX` prefix must be on the component name. The check stream on that path is the harness's third one, `"exception"` (`:136`), whose contents are `ex.toString()` (`:344-345`), prefixed by the command at `:702-704`, so the key is `compile_exception_contains`; no `.test` file in either corpus used an `exception_` key before this one. Pinned, the file is green today (` OK Saw expected exception`, `:347-361`), red when the wall falls (`:382`, then `:395-398`) and red when it moves to a different exception (`:347-348`). First used by `compiler_tests/XXXTryAtomicCodegenRungB.test` for ledger row 353, with `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-2/repair/junit-xxx-tryatomic-expected.txt` and `repair/junit-xxx-tryatomic-goes-red.txt` as the two captures.
- **`testSystem`'s four shards are one suite split by sorted index, so per-shard counts are not comparable across a change to the interpreter corpus and only their sum is** (2026-09-20, the judge on climb batch 2's red gate, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-2/JUDGE-gate.md`). `FileTests.java:790-806` sorts `dir.list()` of `ProjectFortress/tests/` (`:1123`) and keeps index `j` when `j % 4 == i` (root `build.xml:1171-1211`, the `systemShard` macro); a file added to the directory moves every entry that sorts after it along the shards. The landed baseline's 95/95/97/95 (382, `compile-ladder/gate-baseline/summary.txt:49-52`) is the corpus at `a0fcf0a96` (387 entries) and climb batch 2's 98/96/95/95 (384) is the corpus at `8590d7a9e` and at its HEAD (389 entries: `ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss` and `ArrayScalarExtension.fss`, added by `02d09a39f` at sorted positions 5 and 6), both reproduced from the rule alone by `compile-ladder/climb-batch-2/repair/shard-membership.sh` (`shard-membership.txt`); the batch itself added no file to `tests/`. `gate_compare` (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:809-821`) now sums the `system-<i>` rows before comparing; a count that falls on one shard while the sum holds is not red, a count that falls on the sum is.
- **Two constraints of the test and native machinery, measured by rung S** (`6bec1b004`): (1) the native-wrapper generator wraps every method of a class named by `import java`, private ones included, and fails the whole import on any parameter or result type with no Fortress counterpart (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:215-225`, `:250-258`; a `Class<?>` parameter: `compile-ladder/rung-default-rendering/probes/judge-shape-wrapper-error.txt:6`), so a helper in a `nativeHelpers` class needs a Fortress-mappable signature even when private (row 368). ## The library's arrays and algebra

- `Vector[\T extends Number, nat s0\]` and `Matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]` are the only sized array traits; `Array3[\T, nat b0, nat s0, …\]` carries no algebraic trait (row 292; `FortressLibrary.fsi:1465, 1583, 1657` since the library commits of climb batches 3 and 3.5).
- `Vector` and `Matrix` inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero` from `AdditiveGroup`, nothing else; `×` reaches no array by design because juxtaposition is the inner product and the array traits exclude `AnyMultiplicativeRing` (rows 64, 109, 293); a carrier that extends the ring is accepted unchecked, changes juxtaposition to elementwise and breaks `+` (vocabulary review v02, v02b).
- The library's products are declared with shared `nat`s (`Matrix[\T,n,m\]` × `Matrix[\T,m,p\]`, `FortressLibrary.fsi:1508-1516`); C4's own products were not, which is habit; the focused base's `FlatArrays2` states them (twelve declarations including the per-rank elementwise `×` and `/`, 25 of 29 nats agreeing; 39 declarations), and a wrong-shape call is refused at dispatch, uncatchable for an overloaded name (row 83), as a unification error naming the nat for an unoverloaded one (`apl/mg/checks/mismatch_probe.out`).
- Two declarations of one name differing only in the element type, or a rank-specialised declaration beside an index-generic one, are refused at load ("at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"; `apl/mg/checks/model_run.out.0`, `elemwise_nat_probe.out.0`); two apis' overloads of one name are checked as one family, so two vocabularies cannot stand in one component (`diag_fwd_two_vocabularies_rejected.out.0`).
- The shipped `RR64` does not satisfy the specification's algebraic bound `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` (vocabulary review, probe `v04b_groupbound.out.0`); `T extends Number` is the bound that works for every element type and rank (row 295).
- The library's scalar-extension block for `+ - MIN MAX` over arrays is generic since `02d09a39f` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4511-4521`, `.fsi:2550-2560`); no reshape, plane, gather, outer product or ravel exists in the library (vocabulary review, section A).
- An array is a trait with `get`/`put`; a view is an object implementing it over other storage, the language's own idiom; the library's row slice `m[i,:]` costs 5× a six-line user view; a diagonal as a `Matrix` view costs 13-54× the operator (vocabulary review v20, v07); a subtype of `Matrix` that overrides `mul` gets its specialised product through the library's own operators, which forward to `mul` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2627-2633`), at the operator's cost and with no api line, since the interpreter dispatches the method on the receiver's run-time type (2026-09-25, `run-c4/probes/vocabulary/diag-override.md`; ledger row 299).
- The element type is `Number` only for `Vector`/`Matrix` (row 24); irrelevant to numeric microGPT, decisive for Run B's autodiff value and for APL characters.
